lessons.title: What is a port?
lessons.contentHtml:
What is a port?

An IP address finds a computer. A port finds the service running on it, like an apartment number inside a building.

  • 80 HTTP (web, unencrypted)
  • 443 HTTPS (web, encrypted)
  • 22 SSH (secure remote login)
  • 23 Telnet (remote login, not encrypted)
  • 53 DNS (turns names into addresses)

Rule of thumb: every open port is a door. Close the ones nobody needs.

lessons.title: Brute-force attacks
lessons.contentHtml:
Brute-force attacks

A brute-force attack guesses passwords again and again until one works. In logs it looks like many LOGIN_FAIL lines from the same address, often followed by a LOGIN_OK.

How defenders stop it

  • Block or rate-limit the source address
  • Lock accounts after repeated failures
  • Use long passwords and multi-factor authentication

lessons.title: Software Patching
lessons.contentHtml:
Software Patching

Attackers scan for software vulnerabilities with known, unpatched flaws. Blocking an IP only stops one attacker; patching fixes the root vulnerability permanently across your entire infrastructure.
